Building on the model-driven Payne framework, we train an artificial neural network on ~370,000 synthetic spectra spanning FGK stars, and fit the network directly to the flux-calibrated, un-normalised spectral energy distribution (SED) of each star, rather than to a continuum-normalised spectrum as done by DESI's official Stellar Parameter (SP) pipeline. Internal accuracy tests show a median interpolation error of less than 0.3% for 90% of a synthetic verification sample, and the full fitting workflow recovers input labels to high accuracy even at low signal-to-noise ratio (S/N). Validating our method on cross-matched samples of 6719 APOGEE and 3455 GALAH stars observed by DESI with S/N > 20, we recover Teff and logg with smaller systematic offsets than the DESI SP pipeline, an improvement we attribute to fitting the full SED shape rather than a normalised spectrum. We further recover 12 elemental abundances (Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Ni, Ba, and Y) to an accuracy that matches or exceeds SP where a comparison is possible, and provide four abundances, Mn, V, Ba, and Y, that SP does not report at all. Applying this pipeline to the DESI Data Release 1 stellar sample, we deliver a catalogue of stellar parameters and abundances for 3.2 million stars.

title: Multiple H I 21-cm absorbers towards blazar PKS 1158+007
abstract: We report an interesting line of sight towards the blazar PKS 1158+007 (J1201+0028) ($z_{\rm em}$ = 1.369), revealing the rare detection of two intervening HI 21-cm absorption systems within a narrow redshift interval ($Δz \sim 0.04$) using the MeerKAT radio telescope. The stronger absorber at $z_{\rm abs}$ $=0.5653$ ($\intτdv = 1.31\pm0.04$ \kms) is associated with a strong MgII $\lambda2796$ system seen in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectra, with rest-frame equivalent widths of $W_{2796} = 1.40\pm0.07$~Å and $1.21\pm0.11$~Å, respectively. In stark contrast, the second detection at $z_{\rm abs}$ $= 0.5305$ reveals a distinct HI 21-cm absorption feature ($\intτdv = 0.31 \pm 0.04$ \kms) with no associated metal absorption detectable in the optical spectra. This system represents a prime example of a "metal-poor'' HI 21-cm absorber. Using photometric redshifts from Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) PDR3 and DESI Legacy Surveys DR10, we identify a broad galaxy overdensity (at $z \sim0.53\pm0.06$) coincident with these absorbers, suggesting the sightline pierces a complex large-scale structure or filament, which would be interesting to confirm with follow-up observations. These results underscore the power of blind HI 21-cm surveys to uncover the "invisible'' cold gas phase of the Universe that optical/UV metal-line selection may systematically miss.

title: Changing-look Active Galactic Nuclei from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. VII. Testing Disk-Corona Diagnostics with eROSITA
abstract: Changing-look active galactic nuclei (CL-AGN) have been proposed to follow an X-ray-binary-like, V-shaped relation between the optical/ultraviolet-to-X-ray spectral slope, $α_{\rm OX}$, and the Eddington ratio, $λ_{\rm Edd}\equiv L_{\rm bol}/L_{\rm Edd}$. We test this interpretation using CL-AGN selected from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) and control samples matched to the eROSITA all-sky survey (eRASS). We find that the apparent positive correlation between $α_{\rm OX}$ and the optical-continuum-based Eddington ratio, $λ_{\rm Edd,opt}$, is not unique to CL-AGN, but also appears in matched non-changing-look samples. In broad-H$α$ AGN, our main statistical sample, this structure is largely driven by the known dependence of $α_{\rm OX}$ on ultraviolet luminosity and by the covariance between the rest-frame 2500 Angstrom luminosity, $L_{2500}$, the black-hole mass, $M_{\rm BH}$, and $λ_{\rm Edd,opt}$. When an X-ray-based Eddington ratio is used instead, the relation reverses sign because the X-ray luminosity, $L_X$, enters the two axes with opposite signs. An apparent $α_{\rm OX}$-Eddington-ratio V-shape can therefore be induced by the luminosity estimator and is not a standalone accretion-state diagnostic. As a complementary test, we examine the eRASS effective photon index, $Γ_{\rm eff}$, inferred from catalogue band fluxes. In broad-line AGN, it shows a weak positive association with the X-ray-independent optical Eddington ratio. However, the weaker hard-band trend depends on the null model and does not isolate coronal softening. These results motivate further X-ray spectroscopy, combined with independently estimated Eddington ratios, to test for intrinsic changes in the disk-corona system.

title: A Decade-Scale Ionization Echo of Black-Hole Accretion in Galactic Nuclei
abstract: Circumnuclear structures in active galactic nuclei respond to accretion variability over different spatial and temporal scales, but whether compact narrow-line gas responds on decade timescales has not been systematically established. We use repeat Sloan Digital Sky Survey and Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument spectroscopy of 473 variability-selected galactic nuclei with evidence for recent nuclear brightening. We identify 19 sources whose narrow [O III] $\lambda5007$ flux increased by more than a factor of two over rest-frame baselines of 12.0-20.4 yr, which we term narrow-line ionization echoes (NIEs). In equal-weight stacked spectra, [O III] increased by $229\pm22\%$, while lower-ionization lines remained nearly unchanged or declined, indicating an ionization-dependent response rather than uniform spectral rescaling. The NIE hosts also moved coherently toward higher excitation in optical diagnostic diagrams, with mean increases of $0.46\pm0.18$ dex in $\log([\mathrm{O III}]/\mathrm{H}β)$ and $0.58\pm0.13$ dex in $\log([\mathrm{O III}]/[\mathrm{O II}])$. Photoionization models reproduce this evolution with a higher ionization parameter and a harder AGN-like ionizing spectrum at fixed gas abundance. For 13 sources with well-defined mid-infrared outbursts, the integrated W1+W2 excess energy correlates strongly with the absolute [O III] luminosity change ($r=0.87$), linking the dust and narrow-line responses to the same nuclear event. The mid-infrared timescale and spectroscopic baseline constrain the variable [O III]-emitting gas to characteristic scales of 1.5-5.2 pc. Compact narrow-line gas therefore appears to form an intermediate, decade-scale response layer between the infrared dust echo and the long-lived extended narrow-line region.

title: The Population of Type~1 Active Galactic Nuclei in Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument. I. Profile-dependent Measurements of the Low-redshift Sample
abstract: We present a spectral analysis of a large sample of low-redshift type 1 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) selected from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1). For objects at $z\le0.9$, we perform spectral fitting and ML-assisted refinement, yielding 114,754 type 1 AGNs. We use two fitting schemes that differ only in the broad-line model: the broad Balmer components are fitted with either a Lorentzian function or a sum of Gaussians. The continuum and [O III] luminosity measurements agree closely between the two schemes, whereas the Gaussians scheme generally yields larger broad-H$β$ full width at half maximum (FWHM) values, larger virial black hole masses, and lower accretion rates. The adopted broad-Balmer profile also changes the decomposition of narrow Balmer emission. Specifically, the anti-correlation between [O III]$\lambda5007$/narrow H$β$ and accretion rate is stronger under the Gaussians scheme with a Spearman rank correlation coefficient $r_{\rm s}=-0.412$, than under the Lorentzian scheme with $r_{\rm s}=-0.206$; the same tendency is observed in the narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies (NLS1s) subset ($r_{\rm s}=-0.435$ and $-0.259$ for the Gaussians and Lorentzian schemes, respectively), suggesting that the Gaussians scheme may provide a more self-consistent separation of the broad and narrow H$β$ components. Moreover, the consistent correlations recovered under both profile prescriptions favor a continuous type 1 accretion-state sequence, with NLS1s occupying its high-accretion end rather than constituting a distinct population.

title: No-Go Theorem for Phantom Crossing in Scalar-Tensor Gravity with Non-Minimal Derivative Coupling and Soft Scale-Invariance Breaking
abstract: Recent baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI 2024) reveal a preference for dynamical dark energy with an equation of state parameter crossing the phantom divide ($w < -1$) at low redshifts. We investigate whether this phantom crossing can be realized within scale-invariant scalar-tensor theories featuring non-minimal derivative coupling (NMDC) between the scalar field and the Einstein tensor. Employing the effective field theory of dark energy formalism, we systematically derive the ghost-free and gradient stability conditions, and examine their compatibility with the swampland conjectures from quantum gravity. We establish three rigorous no-go theorems demonstrating that: (i)~phantom crossing necessitates $ξ_{\text{eff}} < 0$, directly violating the no-ghost stability requirement $ξ_{\text{eff}} > 0$; (ii)~the swampland de Sitter and distance conjectures independently obstruct phantom crossing; and (iii)~these theoretical obstructions are mutually reinforcing. Our results show that scale-invariant NMDC models cannot account for the DESI preference for $w < -1$, providing robust theoretical guidance for dark energy model building beyond this class.

title: Testing the 4-Point Correlation Function as a Probe of Parity Violation with the Quijote-Odd Simulations
abstract: We investigate parity violation searches with the 4-Point Correlation Function (4PCF) using the Quijote and Quijote-Odd halo catalogs. Specifically, we explore the auto- and cross-correlation searching methodologies that have been previously used in the Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (BOSS) and the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) searches. Although the Quijote-Odd simulations are initialized with a parity-violating primordial trispectrum, we find no statistically detectable parity-odd signal in the halo 4PCF. Instead, we find that the halo measurements are dominated by Poisson noise. We are able to distinguish this noise-dominated behavior from the response expected for a parity-odd signal. These results clarify how parity-sensitive 4PCF statistics respond to noise in a controlled simulation setting.

title: The Pristine survey XXIX. Data Release 2: Photometric metallicities for 15 millions stars down to $G\sim 20.5$
abstract: Tailored narrow-band photometric observations are an efficient way to measure the metallicity of Milky Way stars. The Pristine survey has been mapping the northern sky since 2015 using narrow-band $CaHK$ photometry obtained with the MegaCam imager on the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope (CFHT). Data Release 1 (DR1) provided a high-precision absolute calibration of the survey observed before October 2022 using \Gaia DR3 XP synthetic photometry, yielding photometric metallicities over $\sim$6,500 deg$^2$, but was limited in depth to the availability of \Gaia spectro-photometry ($G \lesssim 17.65$). We present the Pristine Data Release 2 (DR2) that includes all Pristine observations until January 2025, corresponding to an additional 1,500\,deg$^2$ of coverage, and including all faint sources down to $G\sim20.5$. This release aims to exploit the full depth of the Pristine observations to uncover the faint metal-poor halo. We process all images observed from the start of the survey in March 2015 through to January 2025 following the methodology presented in DR1. The core of the calibration utilizes the subset of bright stars with \Gaia synthetic $CaHK_\mathrm{syn}$ magnitudes to train the \texttt{PhotCalib} neural network. We then derive photometric metallicities using the established Pristine ($CaHK, G, G_{\rm BP}, G_{\rm RP}$) to [Fe/H] model. The resulting catalogue covers approximately $\sim$ 8,000 deg$^{2}$ and provides photometric metallicities for 15 millions FGK stars, which show good agreement with recently published, independent Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) metallicities. With its increased coverage and access to a significantly fainter regime compared to DR1, DR2 significantly increases the volume of the survey. We report more than 200,000 and 6,500 very and extremely metal-poor star candidates, respectively.

title: Self Calibrated Galaxy Groups from the DESI DR1 Bright Galaxy Survey
abstract: We present a galaxy group catalog built from Data Release 1 of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Bright Galaxy Survey, using the Self Calibrated Group Finder. The algorithm uses clustering data from the observed sample to calibrate the Group Finder's free parameters, rather than simulations. The catalog contains 2,229,741 galaxies from ~$2680$ deg$^2$ of sky with 3-pass coverage and $r$-band fluxes $\lt 19.5$. The catalog classifies all galaxies in the flux-limited sample as centrals or satellites and estimates host dark matter halo masses. We show the satellite fraction $f_{\rm sat}$, luminosity halo mass relation, stellar halo mass relation and halo occupation distributions (HODs) from the catalog. We find these non-parametric HODs can be fit by standard HOD models, with satellite power-law index $α$ values around 0.75 for star-forming galaxies and around 1.1 for quiescent objects. In agreement with recent results, we find that the quenched fraction of central galaxies depends mostly on halo mass and is nearly independent of central galaxy stellar mass for galaxies more massive than $10^{10.3}$ $M_\odot h^{-1}$ and halos more massive than $10^{12.2}$ $M_\odot h^{-1}$. In an appendix, we introduce a new Hybrid Nearest Neighbor (HNN) technique to mitigate systematics from fiber incompleteness. HNN uses photometric redshifts and multiple on-sky neighbors to assign redshifts to unobserved targets. Calibrated on DESI Survey Validation 3 data, our technique yields correct redshifts $\sim 50\%$ of the time and produces unbiased halo occupation statistics.

title: Star formation history of Draco revealed by DESI DR1: suppressed early star formation efficiency for Milky Way dwarf galaxies
abstract: Dwarf galaxies serve as fossils for understanding the early star formation history of the local Universe. In this work, we use stellar abundances for individual stars derived from the first data release of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI DR1) to investigate the star formation history of the dwarf spheroidal galaxy Draco. We simultaneously fit the stellar metallicity distribution function (MDF) and the [Mg/Fe]-[Fe/H] trend using the galactic chemical evolution (GCE) model flexCE. Our best-fit models imply a low star formation efficiency (SFE) of $0.003$ to $0.007\,\mathrm{Gyr}^{-1}$, which is about ten times lower than values reported in the literature, but consistent with recent SFE estimates for ultra-faint dwarf galaxies. By combining recent literature measurements, we find that the SFEs of Milky Way dwarf galaxies scale with stellar mass as $\mathrm{SFE}\propto M_\star^{0.24}$. A low star formation efficiency is associated with a strong outflow efficiency; we estimate a large wind mass-loading factor $η_{\mathrm{wind}}$ of approximately 172-260. This is well in line with the observed outflow-stellar mass relation and with the Feedback in Realistic Environment (FIRE) cosmological simulations. Our results demonstrate the power of large-scale, low-to-medium resolution stellar spectroscopic surveys to deliver robust constraints on the early formation history of galaxies in the local Universe.

title: A Natural Dark Matter-Dark Energy Interaction from Axion-Monopole Dynamics
abstract: We propose a natural framework for interacting dark matter and dark energy based on axion-monopole dynamics in a dark gauge sector. Dark matter is composed of dark 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles, while dark energy is an ultralight axion whose coupling to the dark gauge field induces an axion-dependent dyon mass through the Witten effect. This generates a direct dark matter-dark energy interaction. We show that generic models with a significant dark matter-dark energy coupling suffer from a naturalness problem: the Coleman-Weinberg potential induced by the interaction is typically much larger than the dark energy scale. In our model, the corrections arise from a monodromy tower of dyon states, allowing them to be exponentially suppressed. In the minimal setup, the interaction strength is predicted to be $\sim 0.1\%$, below the sensitivity of current observations. We discuss scenarios in which cosmological population of higher-charge dyons can enhance the interaction to the percent level, producing an apparent phantom dark energy equation of state. We further show that the parameter space of the axion-monopole model preferred by fitting the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) results can also naturally explain the cosmic birefringence with a small anomaly coefficient.

title: DDELenS: Tomographic Weak Lensing Simulations with Dynamical Dark Energy
abstract: We present a suite of 128 cosmological simulations in $w_0w_a$CDM cosmologies with massive neutrinos, designed to enable simulation-based inference of dynamical dark energy parameters from weak gravitational lensing and other cosmological observables. Each simulation follows $1024^3$ dark matter particles in a $512\,h^{-1}$Mpc periodic box, with cosmological parameters sampled using a Sobol sequence over the ranges $Ω_m \in [0.28, 0.35]$, $σ_8 \in [0.74, 0.90]$, $w_0 \in [-1.0, -0.5]$, and $w_a \in [-1.5, 0.0]$, motivated by recent results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument survey. The nonlinear evolution is computed with $\texttt{PKDGRAV3}$ using the N-body gauge to consistently incorporate relativistic corrections from massive neutrinos, photons, and dark energy. For each cosmology, we generate 10,000 ray-traced convergence maps at six source redshifts $z_s \in \{0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 1100\}$ using $\texttt{LensTools}$, and additionally provide halo catalogues and projected halo overdensity fields for galaxy--lensing cross-correlation analyses. We generate 100,000 realizations at the fiducial cosmology for the construction of the covariance matrix. This simulation suite provides a foundation for field-level inference and non-Gaussian statistics with next-generation weak lensing surveys such as the Rubin Observatory LSST, Euclid, and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, as well as CMB lensing experiments including the Simons Observatory.

title: Alleviating CMB-BAO tension with a large cosmic birefringence angle during reionization induced by energy injection to axion-like particles
abstract: The recent measurement of baryon acoustic oscillations by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument reveals a mild tension with observations of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) within the standard $Λ$CDM cosmological model. Another interesting hint beyond standard cosmology arises from recent analyses of Planck polarization data which has been interpreted as cosmic birefringence. One possible solution to explain both observations is to introduce cosmic birefringence induced by axion-like particles (ALPs) that has a much larger rotation angle during the reionization epoch than that during the recombination: the large rotation suppresses the $EE$ reionization signal, allowing an elevated value of the CMB optical depth $τ$ that alleviates the CMB-BAO tension. In this paper, we explore a scenario where the energy transfers from matter to ALPs before the reionization. Using Planck low-$\ell$ $EE$, $BB$, and $EB$ data, we show that, for energy injection at $10 \lesssim z \lesssim 100$, there exist parameter regions where $τ\simeq 0.08-0.10$ is compatible with the data.

title: Density-split analyses of the pairwise kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect
abstract: We consider the dependence of the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich (kSZ) effect on the environments of foreground cosmological structures. Standard pairwise kSZ estimators exploit the fact that galaxies below separations of $\sim 200\,h^{-1}{\rm M}_\odot$ fall towards each other on average, yielding a negative mean pairwise kSZ signal. However, this signal is the residual from a near-cancellation between outflows from underdense regions and infall towards overdensities giving a large variance in the pairwise velocity distribution and hence a low signal-to-noise ratio for the mean kSZ signal. This effect is especially marked at the largest scales, where the pairwise velocity distribution becomes more symmetric about zero. We show that splitting galaxies according to their local overdensity allows the convergence and divergence flows to be separated, yielding pairwise kSZ signals of opposing sign, with a reduction in variance for each subset. We use simulations to perform a detailed analysis of this phenomenon, comparing the cosmological information content in the global pairwise kSZ signal with our new density-split pairwise kSZ estimator. We consider galaxy catalogues comparable to datasets from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, together with cosmic microwave background instrumental noise characteristic of recent and planned ground-based experiments. We predict that the density-split pairwise kSZ will increase the significance of detection by only a modest factor; nevertheless, we expect improvements by factors of respectively 11 and 4 in constraining $σ_8$ and $Ω_{\rm m}$ when using the combination of Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument and Simons Observatory Large Aperture Telescope surveys.

title: A Catalog of Spectral Properties for DESI DR1 Quasars
abstract: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) is carrying out a five-year spectroscopic survey designed to map the large-scale structure of the Universe and obtain spectra for millions of galaxies and quasars over a wide redshift range. We present a value-added catalog of spectral properties for 1,717,774 unique quasars (1,774,723 spectra) in the DESI Data Release 1. We perform a uniform spectral decomposition of the quasar continuum, host galaxy emission (at $z<1$), and \FeII\ emission, and measure the line properties of major broad and narrow emission lines from Ly$α$ to H$α$ covered by DESI spectra. We also provide single-epoch black hole mass estimates (from H$β$, \MgII, and \CIV), bolometric luminosities, and Eddington ratios for these quasars. We provide systemic redshifts that account for the intrinsic velocity shifts of individual lines; they agree with the DESI pipeline redshifts to within 500~km s$^{-1}$ for 88.6\% of the sample, and are most useful at $z>1$ where the pipeline redshift is heavily constrained by blueshifted high-ionization lines. We also provide local fits to several optical coronal lines, including \NeV~$\lambda3426$, [\ion{Fe}{7}]~$\lambda5722$, [\ion{Fe}{7}]~$\lambda6088$, and [\ion{Fe}{11}]~$\lambda7893$. We show that several emission-line ratios, including those involving coronal lines, vary systematically with Eddington ratio. The catalog is intended as a community resource for studies of quasar demographics, black hole accretion, emission-line physics, and the connection between the broad-, coronal-, and narrow-line regions.
